info.title: Calimero node API
info.description:
Every route a `merod` node serves, on one HTTP API at its `--listen` address. The route table is `router` in `crates/node/src/api.rs`; this document is generated from the registry next to it (`crates/node/src/api/openapi.rs`), whose tests hold it to that table.

**Requests are sealed.** Only `GET /health` and `GET /attestation` travel in the clear. Every other request goes inside the sealed channel (`calimero-sealed`, wire format v2, Noise NK) to the transport key the node's attestation binds, after the client checked the quote against a mero-tee release it trusts; a TDX node refuses plain requests (a node started with `--dev` accepts them). A generic HTTP tool (curl, Postman, a generated client) therefore reaches only those two routes: use a sealing client (`meroctl`, `calimero-client` for Rust, mero-js `CalimeroClient`, calimero-client-py `CloudClient`), or put such a client's transport under the generated code. The paths, bodies and answers below are what travels inside the channel.

**Errors** answer `{ status, error, message, details? }`: `error` is the code, `details` says more (the challenge of a `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED`, the statement of a `428 OPERATOR_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED`, `leaderUrl` of a `421 NOT_LEADER`). Each operation lists the codes it raises itself and those its credential implies, per status in `x-calimero-codes` (every error answer is the one `Error` schema); any operation may also answer `400 BAD_REQUEST`, `400 REJECTED`, `421 NOT_LEADER` and `503 UNAVAILABLE`. A route that takes a session may answer `421 WRONG_NODE` (no `details`): try another node. `x-calimero-details` on an error response maps each of its codes that carries `details` to that value's schema, and `x-calimero-error-details` at the root maps every such code: one code, one schema, so a client reads `details` by `error`.

**Retries.** `x-calimero-retry-safe` marks the operations a client may send again after a `503` or a lost answer (`x-calimero-retry-requires` names the body field that makes it so, an idempotency key). The sealed channel's own `503` (`{ error: { code: "busy", message } }`, outside the envelope: too many sealed requests or sessions at once; the schema `x-calimero-sealed-refusal` names) carries `Retry-After: 1` on any sealed route, and so does `GET /attestation`'s `503 BUSY` (too many quotes at once); the node's `503 UNAVAILABLE` answers carry none. `x-calimero-step-up` (with `x-calimero-user-verification`, and `x-calimero-step-up-when` where it applies only sometimes) and `x-calimero-operator` mark the two-round operations below.

**Numbers** that may exceed 2^53 (fuel, bytes) travel as decimal strings; every other integer is `format: int64` (read it into a 64-bit integer), and stays below 2^53.

post.description:
From a release (`package`, `version`, `service`), a deployment's offer (`deployment`), or an uploaded `bundle`. Every app is in an organization, chosen by the release's signed `instanceOrg` (a raw bundle: `either`): `standalone` makes a new organization with the instance (its name `newOrg.name`, else the instance's), and naming `org` is `400 STANDALONE_INSTANCE`; `org` goes into `org`, else the caller's only organization (`400 ORG_REQUIRED` with several, `409 NO_ORGANIZATION` with none; `newOrg` is `400 ORG_INSTANCE`); `either` goes into `org`, a new one when `newOrg` asks, else the caller's only one, else (none) a new one, `400 ORG_REQUIRED` with several. Below cluster version 1.0.0-rc.32 an instance naming none goes to the caller's personal organization, and `newOrg` is `409 FEATURE_NOT_ACTIVE`. `grants` say who reaches it (#Grant; absent: the organization; empty: the owner alone; any grant needs cluster version 1.0.0-rc.33, `409 FEATURE_NOT_ACTIVE`; the single `access` mode of earlier releases is `400 ACCESS_REMOVED`, never read as no grants). `initArgs` go to the app's `init` and `metadata` is kept as given (both free-form JSON). Answers once `init` committed; `compute` says whether the app has a compute component.

**Who:** an installer (an account holder, or an unscoped API key that is not read-only).

put.summary: Let an app call another as you
put.description:
The methods of `target` that the release `app` runs lists for `target`'s package in its signed `uses` (`methods`), with your passkey over exactly those. You must reach both apps, which are in one organization. From then on, when `app` calls one of those methods while serving you, `target` runs it with you as the caller and reads `env::via()` = `app`; without the grant it runs as `app`, and `target` never learns who `app` was serving. A method that needs your passkey confirmation is still refused there. `409 NOTHING_TO_DELEGATE` when the release lists none. A session opened on an app's frontend is refused (`403`): the app asks on the consent page instead (`POST /consent/requests { kind: "delegate" }`).

**Who:** an account holder (a passkey session not bound to an app's frontend). **Step-up:** answers `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` first; send the same request again with `confirm`, a passkey assertion over `details.challenge`.

get.summary: Where an app's unit may send data
get.description:
For whoever may read the app (`GET /apps/{app}`'s rule). `destinations`: every destination (`outbound` prefix, and a declared secret's host no prefix names) of the release the instance runs and of each app it created with it (`links`, transitively; never an attached app), sorted; empty when no data leaves Calimero. An external endpoint, a TEE included, is listed like any other: the platform never vouches for one (an app that trusts one verifies it in its own code). `members`: each member by its path (`<name>`, a member's own `<name>/<name>`) with its app id, release, signer and own destinations. A development bundle declares none. `egress`: `off` while its organization (`offBy: organization`) or the instance (`instance`) turned egress off (`offBy` and `summary` are absent while it is on), when none of the destinations is reached and `summary` says the app cannot send data outside the cluster.

**Who:** whoever the app's grants admit (`anyone`: any signed-in account).

post.summary: Bring an organization's or account's apps back from its recovery files
post.description:
Sent by the holder's own device, over the sealed channel: its newest `holder` file (`slice`), each app's file and the code files, in the receiving node's `--recovery-dir` (or `--recover-from`) under `org-<id>/` or `account-<id>/`, each with the data key the holder opened from it with its backup key (hex). The cluster admits it with the operator's signature over `cluster / __recover_holder / { holder, slice, apps: [{ app, file, sha256 }] }` (`428` first, naming it). Where owners upgrade apps, and only for an organization, account, apps and passkeys the cluster does not hold; the receiving node seeds each app, which answers `409 APP_RESTORING` until its replicas hold it. People sign in again with the passkeys they had. A pinned app keeps its `lineage` (taken again from its release where the record lost it), and is refused `409 OUTSIDE_LINEAGE` where its package here has another publisher.

**Who:** anyone. **Operator signature:** answers `428 OPERATOR_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED` first; send it again with `operatorProof`, the operator key's signature over `details.message` and its `nonce`.

UnitMember.description: An app of a unit, by its path from the instance: its app id (absent on a release's card, where no app exists), the release it runs or would run, that release's signer, and the destinations it alone may send data to.

UpdateReason.description: Why an update is red (`calimero_bundle::update::Reason`): `member` names a member by its path, `null` for the instance itself. `secretBindingChanged`: the release declares secret `name` it did not (`before` null) or binds it elsewhere (another host or place, or a path its earlier binding did not cover; fewer paths is not a change), each binding in one line. `unclassified`: the release a part runs or moves to (`package`, `version`) is no longer installed, so the update could not be classified and is taken as red. `pinsLineage`: the part, not pinned yet, moves into a release of `package` declaring `lineage: pinned`, so from then on it moves only to that package's newer releases by the same publisher.

RestorePoint.description: An app's one undo (`POST /apps/{app}/undo`): the release and bundle its last upgrade moved it from (`fromRelease`, `fromBundle`) and to, when (`at`, the start of the week to undo it) and by whom (`policy:auto-update` for an update that applied on its own), the run it was part of (a unit's members undo with their instance), the app group's snapshot (`file`: the node that holds it, absent where the upgrade ran nothing on the group) and `undoneAt` while an undo's restore is under way.

consent.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

RestoreConsent.description: An owner's or admin's step-up over `<app> / __restore_older / { backup, sha256, bundle, point }` (`POST /apps/{app}/restore-consent`; `point` is the restore point its open undo would revert, by its time, target and snapshot): the operator's restore carries it as `owner`, with the operator's signature naming the same bundle, to take a pinned instance (its record's `lineage`) from that backup onto that bundle, older than the release it runs, while that undo is open at a time no earlier than the upgrade and any upgrade logged since. Spent once.

UndoPart.description: One app an undo reverts: the release it leaves (`from`) and returns to (`to`, `toBundle`), when it was upgraded and by whom (`auto`: on its own), until when it may be undone, its restore point, and what the undo loses (`lostWrites`: the app group's entries since the restore point, its last write, and `any`: whether it wrote since the upgrade, read from a majority of the replicas the app is on now, the furthest counting, never from the restore point's node alone; each of them `null` when nobody can say, never `false` for writes it cannot see; `lostWrites` itself `null` while the restore point's node does not answer, which `unavailable` then says).

OutboundAuditEntry.description: One outbound request of an instance: `atMs` (Unix milliseconds, the node's clock), `method`, `host` and `path` (no query string, at most 128 bytes, `pathTruncated` when cut; both empty for a URL that did not parse), the host's `status` or, absent that, the `failure` that stopped it (`malformed`, `refused` by a gate, `notApproved`, `awaitingApproval`, `egressOff` (egress turned off), `secret` (a credential binding refused, or a `{{secret:` placeholder), `failed` in transit), the names of the credential bindings the node attached in `secrets` (for a `secret` refusal, the binding refused), and the request's and response's body sizes. Never a secret value, a body, a query string or a header.

OutboundLog.description: An instance's outbound requests, newest first (`entries`), merged from every replica; `partial`: a replica did not answer, so its runs' requests may be missing.

runs.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

fuel.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

wallMs.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

writes.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

bytesWritten.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

events.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

UsageDay.description: What an app's runs used on one UTC day (`date`, `YYYY-MM-DD`), each figure a decimal string; `wallMs` is information only.

RunFile.description: A file a run reads or wrote: its id, and its plaintext size and SHA-256 (hex) only for a caller who may list the app's files.

items.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Run.description: A compute run's record, without its arguments or keys: its method, state, caps (`fuel` a JSON number here), inputs, attempts (`tsMs` Unix milliseconds) and final outcome (`null` while it runs; `message` the failure text, `null` unless the caller may list the app's files). `progress` is the leader's last poll (`null` elsewhere, when it is not active, or to a caller who may not list files); `queue` where the run waits for a job node, to a caller who may list files only; `logs` (deprecated: a run keeps no log) is always empty, to the same callers.

AccountProof.description: A statement, signed with the answering node's receipt key (hex, Ed25519 over the statement's canonical JSON after its domain), that the account asked to bind `nonce` for `audience`, valid from `issuedAt` to `expiresAt` (Unix seconds).

AccountStatement.description: What an account proof states: the cluster and node, the account, the nonce and audience it binds, and when it was issued and expires (Unix seconds).

PackageOrigin.description: A custom frontend origin of a package: the rp-id its passkeys use, who registered it and when (RFC 3339), and whether the cluster serves the package's frontend there.

SignUpState.description: The sign-up policy and what it implies: whether organization invites and cluster sign-up invites admit a new account, and whether one is required.

ApprovedReleases.description: The mero-tee releases the scope approves now, after the change.

OutboundApproved.description: The outbound approval the scope holds now for the package's publisher (`signer`), after the change.

Deadlines.description: Every release deadline after the change, oldest release first (`after` RFC 3339, `afterSecs` Unix seconds).

SignUpSet.description: The cluster's governance and sign-up policy after the change.

InviteKey.description: The key of the cluster sign-up invite withdrawn.

UpgradeRun.description: An organization-wide upgrade run: the apps it targets, those done, and why each failed one failed.

initArgs.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

App.description: An app instance as the directory records it. `executor` is absent for an SDK 0.12 app (wasmer), which this node lists but does not run; `release` is the package release it runs, absent for a record from before or a raw upload; `restore` is a restore from a backup under way; `restorePoint` the restore point of its last upgrade, which an owner or admin may undo for a week (`POST /apps/{app}/undo`); `egressOff`: the instance's own egress switch is off (`POST /apps/{app}/egress`), absent while on; `lineage`: the package and signer a release declaring `lineage: pinned` pinned it to, and `floor`, the newest version it has been judged at, absent while unpinned: it moves only to releases of that package, never one older than `floor`.

AppEntry.description: An app as `GET /apps` lists it: `package` and `version` name the release it runs where the caller may read it (`null` otherwise, and for a raw upload); `?package=` keeps the instances whose row names that package, `deployment` the deployment it was created from (`null` for none; absent from an older node, as 1.0.0-rc.1).

PackageRef.description: One service of one package release: `service` is absent for a single-service bundle, `compute` (absent: false) marks the service's compute component.

error.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Upgrade.description: The last upgrade tried on an app, done or failed: `from` and `to` are bundle hashes, `by` the account (or `operator`), `run` the organization-wide run it was part of, `apiKey` the upgrade key that made it. `class` and `reasons`: what the update classifier said of it, judged again where it applied (absent before cluster version 1.0.0-rc.34, for a raw bundle and a failed upgrade); `approvedBy`: the first approver of a red update whose policy asks for a second. `auto`: it applied on its own under the app's update policy (`by` is `policy:auto-update`); `undo`: it undid the upgrade before it (`fromRelease` the release undone).

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Package.description: A package and the releases of it the caller may see, oldest first; `latest` is the newest of those. A release's `visibility`: `public` (everyone here uses it; a release the operator installed, the cluster's catalog, is always), `private` (members of the organizations it was installed for; none: the accounts that installed it), absent for one recorded before the node kept it. `orgs`: of a private release's organizations, only those the caller is a member of.

ApiKey.description: An API key as the account's list shows it (never its secret): `apps` and `methods` are `null` for every one; `upgrades` makes it an upgrade key.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Org.description: An organization as `GET /orgs/{org}` answers it. `members` maps each account to its role, `capabilities` and `defaultCapabilities` are capability bits, `outboundApprovals` is keyed by package signer, `upgradeRuns` by run id; `recovery` is absent when the organization set no recovery key, `allApps` when no member gets every app added later, `personal` unless it is a personal organization a sign-up made before cluster version 1.0.0-rc.33 (from that version it is an organization like any other). `allowGuests`: whether its instances take guests (its owner or an admin sets it, `POST /orgs/{org}/settings`; absent from a node before 1.0.0-rc.33). `egressOff`: its egress switch is off, so none of its apps sends anything out of the cluster (`POST /orgs/{org}/egress`). `upgradePolicy`, `appUpgradePolicies` and `pendingUpgrades`: its update policy, its apps' own and the first approvals of red updates waiting for a second (absent when none).

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Team.description: A team as its organization records it: `members` maps each direct row to whether it is a lead; `capabilities` are capability bits per row; `defaultCapabilities` is absent when unset.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

TeamView.description: A team as `GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team}` answers it: each member's row, the child teams the caller sees, its apps, and the caller's own row (`myRole`, `null` for none) and membership (`member`). `package` names the package of an app team (`null` for any other), `defaultCapabilities` the capabilities a new member gets (`null`: the organization's).

Deployment.description: A deployment as its managers list it. `host` is its frontend host, `null` on a node with no apps domain; times are RFC 3339. `transfer`: the offer of it to another owner waiting for acceptance (`expiresAt`: 7 days after `offeredAt`), else `null`; `transferred`: whom it came from at its last hand-over, else `null`.

DeploymentShown.description: The deployment an instance comes from, as its customers are shown it: names are not unique, so always with its id and its owner's kind and name (`null` once the owner is gone); once it changed hands, whom it came from and when (`transferred`, RFC 3339).

DeadLetter.description: A cross-app call that was never delivered: its sequence number, the target app and method, why, and when (`atMs`, Unix milliseconds).

Governance.description: Who decides what on this cluster: release approvals, app upgrades and outbound approvals (`owner`: each app's owner; `operator`: the operator), and, left out at their defaults, `deployments` (`open`), `deployers` (`operator`) and `signUp` (`open`).

OutboundApproval.description: What an owner approved for one publisher's apps to call out to: the approved URL prefixes, and every prefix it was shown.

AppScope.description: The scope whose approvals cover an app: its organization (`personal: true` when it is its owner's personal organization, below cluster version 1.0.0-rc.32 only). `account` is only `GET /auth/apps`' own scope: the apps the account owns, wherever they are.

ClusterRelease.description: A mero-tee release the cluster's nodes run: how many run it, and whether the scope approved it (`true` where nothing was ever recorded).

BundleRelease.description: A bundle by its digest, with the release it came from where the reader may see it.

error.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

ReportUpgrade.description: An app's last upgrade as a report shows it. `actor`, `error`, `run` and `apiKey` are shown to the app's people, never to the operator.

ReportApp.description: One app in a release report (`GET /auth/apps`, `GET /orgs/{org}/apps`, `GET /ops/apps`): its bundle and release (`package`, `null` where the reader may not see it), the publisher's key and bound organization, who holds its upgrades and release approvals, its last upgrade, the releases approved to hold it (`null`: unrestricted), each replica's release, and `lastWriteAt` (Unix seconds, `null` when unknown). `name`, `team`, `availableVersions` (newer releases, oldest first), `latestReachable` and `latestBlocked` (the newest release and why an upgrade would not take it) are for the app's people, never the operator.

DeploymentRecord.description: A deployment as the directory records it: the release it offers by app name (`addedAt` Unix seconds), who created it and when (Unix seconds).

DeployerGrant.description: A grant to install where deployments are granted: until when (Unix seconds; absent: it does not end), when and by whom it was granted.

SignUpInvite.description: A cluster sign-up invite, never its token: uses left, when it expires (`expiresAt` RFC 3339, `expiresAtSecs` Unix seconds), who made it and when (RFC 3339).

ProofOnly.description: What an operator decision that names nothing in its body may carry: none at first, the operator's proof after the `428`.

ConfirmOnly.description: The body of a step-up that names nothing else: none (or `{}`) at first, the passkey assertion after the `412`.

orgs.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

maxFuelPerDeveloperPerDay.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

computeFuel.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string, exact past 2^53

QuotaChanges.description: The limits `POST /ops/quotas` changes, each optional: without `org`, the cluster's (those `GET /ops/quotas` answers, `maxFuelPerDeveloperPerDay` a decimal string); with `org`, one payer's (`maxConcurrentRuns`, `computeFuel` a decimal string, `maxFileBytes`; `null` clears one). `orgs` is ignored. Any other property is refused `400 UNKNOWN_QUOTA`.

session.description: A passkey session's token (15 minutes, by the issuing node), from a passkey ceremony or `/auth/refresh`.

apiKey.description: An API key from `POST /auth/apikeys`, scoped to apps, methods and read-only as made.
